# CDB OpenTakeoff — Ductape-Build downstream fork

This app and MCP are independent of the official Kentucky AI distribution. Build `cdb-development` locally; `cdb-opentakeoff-mcp` is private and not published on npm. See the CDB setup guide below. Upstream licensing and wire identifiers remain intact.

> Free, open-source (AGPL-3.0) construction takeoff engine that a person and an AI agent drive the same way. Open a plan (PDF, image, or .zip plan set), set the scale, trace areas with a 45°/90° angle lock, then apply waste % and per-condition supporting materials, and export quantities (SF/SY/LF/EA) as CSV/JSON. A person clicks the canvas; an agent calls the identical engine over MCP (`node mcp/dist/server.js` from the repository root) and gets the identical number, with the scale and origin of every measurement recorded. Built for flooring; the measuring engine works for any trade (drywall, paint, concrete, sitework). No account, no upload: the canvas keeps plans in the browser.

OpenTakeoff is an open-source alternative to subscription takeoff software — and the first takeoff engine an AI agent can drive natively, not through screen scraping or a bolted-on chat layer. It is a static web app: self-hosting is one `npm run build` and any static file host.

## Key facts

- **Agent-native**: the same engine answers to a person at the canvas or an AI agent over MCP — not two implementations, one. Every shape records its provenance: scale, method, and person or agent.
- **MCP server**: private `cdb-opentakeoff-mcp`, local source build, <!--tool-count-->65<!--/tool-count--> tools on a default build, plus trade-suite tools (roofing, siding, soffit and fascia, glazing, plumbing, electrical) an agent opens one trade at a time — an agent loads a plan, reads the title block, adopts the scale (never applied silently), traces rooms on the wall faces, and exports the same payload the app autosaves.
- Measuring: Area, Rectangle, Linear, Surface-Area (walls), Count, Deduct. One-Click Area (flood-fill room detection) is temporarily gated while it is re-validated; `VITE_ONE_CLICK=1` / `OPENTAKEOFF_ONE_CLICK=1` lift the gate
- Drawing aids: 45°/90° angle lock (polar tracking with ⇧ hard-lock, commits the on-axis point), live angle + segment-length readout at the cursor, endpoint snap
- Scale: auto-detects the drawn scale note per sheet, or calibrate from a known dimension
- Conditions: color + CAD hatch per finish, waste %, multiplier, wall height, border thickness
- Assemblies: per-condition supporting materials with coverage rates → rounded order quantities
- Reports: per-condition SF/SY/LF/EA with and without waste + a materials buy list; CSV/JSON export
- Storage: IndexedDB + localStorage only — client-side, private by construction
- Stack: React 18 + Vite + pdf.js; the whole app is a static build
- License: AGPL-3.0-only — [fork it](https://github.com/Kentucky-ai/opentakeoff/fork), ship it, build a product on it, and publish your changes when you run a modified copy for others (Apache-2.0 through commit 84c7f48e). Pull requests from a fork run the full CI; tested PRs from agents merge under the same bar as anyone's
- CDB fork maintained by Ductape-Build: https://github.com/Ductape-Build/opentakeoff
- Upstream OpenTakeoff by Kentucky AI (applied AI R&D, Louisville, KY): https://kentucky-ai.com
- Normal tools use a separate offline session; explicit live-browser tools require opt-in connectivity and identity checks. Neither shared math nor chat pairing proves live-canvas connectivity.
